name: AApoAI Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Demonstration of amyloid deposits with Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the APOA1 gene
Presence of characteristic organ involvement such as renal, hepatic, or cardiac amyloid deposition
Immunohistochemical confirmation of apolipoprotein AI in amyloid deposits

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of amyloid deposits plus either pathogenic APOA1 mutation or characteristic organ involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic counseling is recommended for affected families.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive renal amyloid deposition causing proteinuria and renal insufficiency
searchTerms: progressive kidney failure with protein in urine

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cutaneous amyloid deposits presenting as nodules or plaques
searchTerms: raised skin plaques due to amyloid

common.symptomName: Restrictive cardiomyopathy with heart failure symptoms
Peripheral neuropathy with sensory and motor deficits
searchTerms: nerve damage causing numbness and weakness
peripheral nerve loss of feeling and strength

common.symptomName: Orthostatic hypotension secondary to autonomic neuropathy
searchTerms: dizziness when standing due to nerve damage

occasional.symptomName: Carpal tunnel syndrome from amyloid deposits in flexor retinaculum
searchTerms: wrist nerve compression from protein deposits
carpal tunnel symptoms due to amyloid
general feeling of illness with weight loss

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary amyloid nodules causing respiratory symptoms
searchTerms: amyloid lumps in lungs causing symptoms

rare.symptomName: Ocular amyloid deposits leading to vitreous opacities
searchTerms: amyloid in eye causing vision changes

rare.symptomName: Gastrointestinal bleeding due to amyloid infiltration of the bowel wall
searchTerms: blood in stool from bowel wall damage

laboratory: Serum amyloid P component scintigraphy showing amyloid deposits
imaging: MRI neurography demonstrating peripheral nerve involvement
other: Congo red staining of biopsy specimens with apple-green birefringence
Immunohistochemical staining positive for apolipoprotein AI

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in TTR gene instead of APOA1
Predominant neuropathy and cardiomyopathy without significant renal involvement
Presence of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine
Rapidly progressive cardiac and renal failure

redFlags: Rapidly progressive proteinuria and renal failure
Unexplained hepatomegaly with abnormal liver function tests
Restrictive cardiomyopathy in a patient with family history of amyloidosis
references: Merlini G, Bellotti V. Molecular mechanisms of amyloidosis. N Engl J Med. 2003;349(6):583-596.
Gertz MA. Hereditary amyloidosis: the importance of early diagnosis. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2015;2015:1-7.
